cards.question: What is deep-seek-harness, and what does one launch of it produce?
cards.answer: A launcher: one command runs the pinned upstream `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and opens its Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080`.
cards.explanation: The repository holds NO agent code of its own: two launcher scripts, a `package.json` with the pinned dependency and a README runbook. The agent harness is downloaded at launch.
cards.anchor: An ignition key with no car attached: turn it and the same rented car is delivered to your driveway, engine running, doors open.
cards.example: ./start-harness.sh  # browser opens the harness Web UI on loopback port 3080
cards.evidence_quote: "description": "Local launcher for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080"

cards.question: Which one-sentence rule does deep-seek-harness enforce about the upstream release it launches?
cards.answer: It launches the release the setup was last VERIFIED against (the pin), never the newest one by default.
cards.explanation: Upstream is a fast-moving developer preview, so a newer release may change flags or first-run steps. Breaks if undone: a launch that worked yesterday fails without any change here. The newest release is an explicit opt-in, see 10.
cards.confusables: `@latest` — tracks whatever upstream published last; the pin tracks what was TESTED here.
cards.evidence_quote: # Version this setup was verified against; override with DSH_VERSION=latest for the newest release.

cards.question: Which environment variable makes deep-seek-harness launch another upstream release for a single run?
cards.answer: `DSH_VERSION`, e.g. `DSH_VERSION=latest ./start-harness.sh`; left unset, each script uses its pinned default.
cards.explanation: Both launcher scripts read it and fall back to their own hard-coded default. Nothing is edited on disk, so the next plain launch is back on the pin.
cards.confusables: the `package.json` dependency version — `DSH_VERSION` steers ONLY the two launcher scripts; `pnpm start` never reads it.
cards.example: DSH_VERSION=latest ./start-harness.sh  # newest upstream release, this run only

cards.question: deep-seek-harness · `start-harness.sh`: recite the 5 steps from the call to the process that replaces the shell.
cards.answer: node present · major at least 22 · resolve `DSH_VERSION` · first-run notice · `pnpm dlx`, else `npx -y`
steps: `command -v node` -> missing: error on stderr and `exit 1`
`node -p` extracts the Node major -> below 22: error on stderr and `exit 1`
`DSH_VERSION` -> kept when set, otherwise the pinned default
`echo` -> notice that the first run downloads the package
`command -v pnpm` -> found: `exec pnpm dlx`; missing: hint, then `exec npx -y`
cards.explanation: Both guards run BEFORE anything is downloaded, so a missing or old Node fails fast with a readable message. The last step uses `exec`, so the package manager takes over the shell's process and Ctrl+C in the terminal stops the server.
cards.anchor: A launch-pad countdown: is there an engine, is it a recent enough model, load the flight number, announce a long fuelling, then light the fast booster or, failing that, the slow one.

cards.question: Which script do you run first to open the deep-seek-harness Web UI on macOS or Linux, and from which directory?
cards.answer: `start-harness.sh`, run FROM the project the agent should work in: that directory becomes the default workspace root.
cards.explanation: Windows uses `start-harness.cmd` the same way. Launched from inside the launcher's own checkout, the agent's default workspace is the launcher itself, not your project.
cards.example: cd ~/my-project && /path/to/deep-seek-harness/start-harness.sh  # my-project becomes the default workspace root
cards.evidence_quote: From the directory you want the agent to work in (that directory becomes the default workspace root):

cards.question: deep-seek-harness · `start-harness.sh`: predict the exact command that replaces the shell for the call below.
cards.code_snippet:
# pnpm is installed; DSH_VERSION is not set
# call: ./start-harness.sh --port 4000 --no-open
DSH_VERSION="${DSH_VERSION:-0.1.1-rc.2}"
# ...
if command -v pnpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exec pnpm dlx "@deepseek-ai/dsh@${DSH_VERSION}" web "$@"
else
  # ...
  exec npx -y "@deepseek-ai/dsh@${DSH_VERSION}" web "$@"
fi
cards.answer: `pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2 web --port 4000 --no-open` — the default fills the unset variable and every script argument is APPENDED after `web`.
cards.explanation: (1) `DSH_VERSION` is unset, so `:-` yields the default. (2) pnpm is found, so the first branch runs. (3) `"$@"` expands to the two flags, placed after the `web` subcommand, which is where upstream expects its flags.
cards.confusables: the `npx -y` branch — same package, same `web` and the same forwarded flags; it runs ONLY when pnpm is absent.

cards.question: deep-seek-harness: `start-harness.sh` vs `start-harness.cmd`: what is the ONE difference in what they verify before launching?
cards.answer: `start-harness.sh` checks that Node exists and that its major is at least 22; `start-harness.cmd` checks ONLY that `node` is on PATH.
cards.explanation: The batch file runs `where node` and nothing more, so on Windows the launcher stops no Node version at all. For how loose the sh guard itself is, see 92.
cards.confusables: `start-harness.cmd` — NO version guard: any Node that is on PATH gets through the Windows launcher.
cards.anchor: Two doormen: one reads the birth year on your card, the other only checks that you are holding a card.

cards.question: Which deep-seek-harness command runs the harness from an INSTALLED dependency instead of a download-and-run?
cards.answer: `pnpm start`, after `pnpm install`: the `package.json` script `"start": "dsh web"`.
cards.explanation: It runs the `dsh` binary of the dependency declared in `package.json`, so its release is whatever that file pins, independent of the launcher scripts (see 91).
cards.confusables: `./start-harness.sh` — runs `@deepseek-ai/dsh@$DSH_VERSION` EPHEMERALLY through dlx or npx; `pnpm start` runs the copy in `node_modules`.
cards.example: pnpm install / pnpm start  # runs: dsh web

cards.question: Why does deep-seek-harness launch through `pnpm dlx` whenever pnpm is installed rather than always using `npx -y`?
cards.answer: npm's resolver can stall for a very long time on the package's large release-candidate dependency graph; pnpm resolves the same graph in seconds.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: the first launch sits on 'resolving dependencies' and looks frozen. `npx -y` survives ONLY as the fallback, and the scripts print a hint to install pnpm before taking it.
cards.confusables: `npx -y` — the same download-and-run idea, but through npm's resolver; kept as the FALLBACK only.
cards.anchor: Two couriers are handed the same enormous parts list: one sorts it at the counter in seconds, the other stands chewing his pencil until closing time.
cards.evidence_quote: resolver can grind for a very long time, so prefer pnpm when it is available.

cards.question: Why does deep-seek-harness reach a harness on a remote machine through an SSH port-forward rather than a public tunnel such as ngrok?
cards.answer: Nothing authenticates the Web UI, and its API tells an agent to run shell commands in the workspace: ANYONE who reaches the port can execute code on the machine.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: a published port is an open shell on your workspace. The server therefore stays on `127.0.0.1`, and the README notes that upstream itself refuses `--host 0.0.0.0`. The forward command: see 81.
cards.confusables: a public tunnel or a reverse proxy on a public interface — it publishes the port to EVERYONE; an SSH forward opens it only to the holder of the SSH login.
cards.anchor: A workshop with no lock and an obedient robot inside that does whatever a visitor tells it: it is kept in a windowless back room reached only by your own private corridor.
cards.evidence_quote: its API drives an agent that can execute shell commands in your workspace

cards.question: What makes the Web UI launched by deep-seek-harness able to call the DeepSeek API, and through which two routes is it supplied?
cards.answer: A DeepSeek API key: pasted under Settings -> Models in the Web UI, or set as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in a `.env` in the directory you LAUNCH from.
cards.explanation: The key never lives in the repository: `.gitignore` excludes `.env` and only the empty template `.env.example` is tracked. Because the file is read from the invoking directory, a `.env` beside the script is missed when you launch from another project.
cards.confusables: cf. [private project] `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`: there it is ONE provider key among several for a Hermes agent; here it is the only secret the setup needs.
cards.evidence_quote: # Copied to .env (git-ignored), this is picked up by dsh from the invoking directory.

cards.question: deep-seek-harness: complete the SSH command that brings a harness running on a remote box to your local browser.
cards.explanation: Local port 3080 is forwarded to loopback port 3080 on the remote box, where the server listens; you then open `http://127.0.0.1:3080` locally. Why this route and not a tunnel: see 61.

cards.question: deep-seek-harness has no test suite: which manual check proves a launch works, and what is its passing sign?
cards.answer: Launch with `--no-open`, then request `http://127.0.0.1:3080`: HTTP 200 and the app renders.
cards.explanation: This is the only verification the repository records: one end-to-end run on a clean Linux container. Nothing automated guards a broken upstream release.
cards.example: ./start-harness.sh --no-open  # then fetch http://127.0.0.1:3080 and expect HTTP 200
cards.evidence_quote: served the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080 (HTTP 200, app renders)

cards.question: deep-seek-harness: you run `npm run update:dsh` to move to a newer upstream release. Which launch path now runs the new release, and which still runs the old one?
cards.answer: ONLY `pnpm start` moves, because the script rewrites the `package.json` dependency. `start-harness.sh` and `start-harness.cmd` still launch the old release: each carries its own hard-coded `DSH_VERSION` default.
cards.explanation: The pin lives in THREE files and the update script touches one. Fix: edit both script defaults in the same change, or use `DSH_VERSION=latest` for a one-off run. Note that the script goes through npm, the resolver the launchers avoid (see 60).
cards.confusables: `DSH_VERSION=latest` — changes ONE run of the launcher scripts and writes nothing; `update:dsh` rewrites `package.json` and leaves the scripts alone.
cards.example: npm run update:dsh  # package.json dependency changes; the two script defaults do not

cards.question: deep-seek-harness documents Node 22.19+ or 24+ as its requirement. Which Node versions does `start-harness.sh` actually refuse to launch with?
cards.answer: ONLY majors below 22. The guard compares the major number alone, so 22.0 to 22.18 pass it although they sit below the documented 22.19 minimum.
cards.explanation: The script extracts the first component of the Node version and tests it with `-lt 22`; the minor is never read (23.x passes too). Check `node --version` by hand against the documented rule. The Windows launcher has no version test at all, see 40.
cards.confusables: the documented requirement `22.19+ or 24+` — it constrains the minor as well; the guard reads the MAJOR only.

cards.question: deep-seek-harness pins a release candidate of a fast-moving developer preview. You return after months: what is the first step, and what must change together if it passes?
cards.answer: Re-verify against the newest upstream before trusting the runbook. (1) Run `DSH_VERSION=latest ./start-harness.sh --no-open` and expect HTTP 200 on `http://127.0.0.1:3080`. (2) If it passes, move the pin in ALL three files: both script defaults and the `package.json` dependency. (3) If it fails, stay on the pin: the documented flags and first-run steps are only known to hold for that release.
cards.explanation: The repository records no roadmap; this step follows from its own statements: the pin is the last verified release, upstream changes fast, and the override exists to try the newest release without editing anything. Why all three files: see 91.
cards.evidence_quote: DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and changes fast.
